body.statement: Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\) and \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the law of the vector \((T_{B,n}(\tau))_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\) consistently estimates the limit in \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\). For every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the pointwise interval \[\left[\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau),\;\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)\right]\] has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\). For local unequal-heavy-tail sequences whose index gap has exact order \(1/\log n\), raw scalar QTE subsampling at any fixed polynomial rate strictly between constant and linear generally converges to the wrong arm mixture.
body.justification: Armwise refitting reproduces first-stage uncertainty and repairs the near-equal-index scalar-mixture failure.
body.gap: Heiler and Kazak treat scalar mean-type irregular statistics, not two learned convex argmins with unequal arm scales.
body.consumer: The theorem yields the displayed implementable pointwise confidence interval for each reported quantile across heavy, mixed, and Gaussian QTE regimes.
